import re def parse_html_tags(html: str) -> list[str]: """ Extract all HTML tags from the input string. Parameters ---------- html : str The input HTML content. Returns ------- list[str] A list of all tags found in the input string. Each tag includes its surrounding angle brackets (e.g., '
', ''). Notes ----- - The implementation uses a non-greedy pattern that matches any sequence of characters that does not contain the closing angle bracket. - No exceptions are raised; malformed input simply results in an empty list or a subset of matched tags. """ if not isinstance(html, str): # Gracefully handle non-string input return [] # Pattern explanation: # < : literal opening bracket # [^>]*? : any number of characters except '>' (non-greedy) # > : literal closing bracket tag_pattern = re.compile(r"<[^>]*?>", re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL) return tag_pattern.findall(html)
